correctness.rationale: The Gaifman degree of a successor path is at most two, so effective bounded-degree Hanf locality gives a radius and count cap for each fixed rank. Short endpoint balls are fixed by the two length-(2r+1) boundary words; full balls are binary windows. Each interior pattern has linearly many independent disjoint trials in the seed, each of fixed positive success probability. A binomial tail and union bound give simultaneous saturation except with exponentially small probability. Reversal permutes the full-window types; internal seams can only add to a saturated count. For n>2(2r+1), equal endpoint signs use disjoint seed windows, whereas opposite signs give a uniform window and its reverse. Couple the exact boundary laws before discarding the marginal failure probabilities; this proves exponential rank-theory TV even across different fixed copy counts. A long inserted block containing all patterns repeatedly gives a computable representative for each admissible boundary pair. Uniform averaging gives dyadic values, and prefix tests realize all dyadics. Endpoint bit equality separates the two phases; injectivity of the first block gives TV exactly 1−2^(-(m−1)n) for full words. Independent bounded replay passed 336 endpoint cases, 196 injectivity cases, 36 full-word-TV cases and 16 capped-local-profile comparisons.
residual_risks: Bounded replay checks examples rather than Hanf locality or convergence rates. The proof is for fixed rank and the immediate-successor vocabulary, with no order or named copy boundaries.
